In a letter to fans, a defiant Khaldoon Al Mubarak, City’s chairman, expresses complete confidence that his club would be vindicated.

“There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club,” he writes. “We will not give them that opportunity.”

With the football world still making sense of the news, Tony Pulis admits to feeling “cheated”. His Stoke City side were defeated by Manchester City in the 2011 FA Cup final, during the 2009-23 period.

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali then likens City’s transgressions to “doping” before Mauricio Pochettino, whose Spurs side were often in the hunt with City for major trophies during his time as manager, says that football has “lived through a period of deception”.

The Premier League reveals that City’s owners inflated “sham” sponsorship deals by £830.69m between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

It also discloses that image rights had been inflated and key witnesses had lied.

Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group, appears helpless when questioned about the verdict’s findings at the European Football Clubs’ general assembly in Copenhagen by Sky News.

An unblinking Soriano then features in a video statement published by City in which he claimed their guilty verdict was based on “a single false accusation”.

With City on the ropes, Pep Guardiola releases a statement in support of his former club, assuring supporters that “we will get through this together”.

The Prime Minister says that he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s owners, but after significant backlash, No 10 moves to clarify his reaction saying that “if wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences”.

It later amends the statement to “wherever wrongdoing is established”.

The UAE then warns Andy Burnham that it will pull billions of pounds of investment out of the UK in retaliation for the guilty verdict against City.

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission said. I think that’s what’s worried me.”

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

#1553. GdS: A red-hot start and the ‘S’ word – the data that inspires confidence in Amorim

A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

His style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri currently sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

It is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

However, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

Gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

To date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the new era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target announced by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

In third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

In short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

#1551. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

#1549. Musah lifts lid on Amorim’s faith, early career, preferred role and Scudetto ‘ambition’

Yunus Musah has insisted that AC Milan must believe in the Scudetto, while also assessing his start to the campaign under Ruben Amorim.

Going into the summer, an uncertain fate awaited Musah. Massimiliano Allegri did not see him as a part of the plans for 2025-26 and so he was loaned to Atalanta, where he had a mixed year and ultimately returned as they did not use their option to buy him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Many sources presumed that it would be a return in passing and that a new destination would be found, but Amorim had other plans. The new coach clearly saw something in the USA international, and he has become a regular starter regardless of the system used.

Such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

“A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”

“I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

“I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

“I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”

Do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

“It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

“Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”

“I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

“Yes, in 2021 I returned to New York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”

“Yes. I left him with the neighbours in Valencia because I couldn’t take him to Milan.”

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

“Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

“Of course. Obviously, when I grew up, we weren’t rich, we didn’t have much money, but from the time I left home, even when I was little, my parents never let me go without anything. I hope I’m their pride, because they are mine.”

You have also played for Arsenal and Valencia. What were the transitions like?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

“I was ready to move to the first team when I was 16, and Valencia had a plan for me. I spent four wonderful years in Spain; it’s a city that will always remain in my heart.”

What’s the atmosphere like in the dressing room?

“Last year I watched them a lot; they were a very solid team and difficult to beat. Amorim brought a very positive vibe, we understand each other. He understands the player very well and vice versa.

“It helps when he understands what the players need; he’s good at that, and the players in the team are pretty calm.”

Is he someone who gets angry when necessary?

“Yes. After Ferencvaros he was very angry, like everyone else.”

“My wife is from Zanzibar, my family is Ghanaian. So it’s nice to travel to our home countries in the summer.”

#1548. Nico Paz compared to Messi and Maradona amid Real Madrid return rumours

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 20:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:01

Real Madrid's reported plans to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.

Los Blancos are reportedly preparing to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option for the Como playmaker next summer, having watched his remarkable development under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, Madrid have decided to exercise the clause, which can only be triggered during the summer 2027 transfer window.

The 22-year-old has scored six goals and provided eight assists in 14 club appearances this season, establishing himself as one of the most influential attacking midfielders in Italian football.

However, Veron's latest assessment of Paz offers more than an extraordinary comparison with two of Argentina's greatest players.

The former Argentina international has also emphasised the importance of regular football in developing young talents, a consideration that could become significant if Paz returns to a Madrid squad already containing Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler.

Speaking in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, Veron reserved exceptional praise for Paz after the midfielder continued his impressive international development.

"Nico Paz has incredible talent. He is destined for great things," the former Manchester United midfielder said. "The future belongs to him if he continues to behave like a professional, as he is doing."

Veron then made a particularly striking comparison. "At 22, I have only seen Messi and a certain Diego Armando Maradona do certain things like that."

The 51-year-old was careful not to suggest that Paz was guaranteed to reach the extraordinary heights achieved by either legend. "I don't mean that he will reach those levels, but he has the qualities to attempt it," Veron explained.

What particularly impresses the former Chelsea midfielder is the confidence Paz displays when receiving possession under pressure.

Veron highlighted the youngster's ability to dictate the rhythm of attacks, move into dangerous positions and retain the trust of his teammates even when closely marked.

Rather than describing him solely as an individual talent, he identified Paz as the player around whom Como organise much of their attacking football.

"Nico is a leader in the way he manages moves. He is the focal point of the game," Veron added.

Those qualities have become increasingly apparent under Fabregas, whose possession-based approach has allowed the Argentine to develop into a central figure.

Paz has also carried his club form onto the international stage. He recently scored twice for Argentina against Costa Rica, further strengthening his credentials as one of the country's leading young talents following Messi's international retirement.

His performances have inevitably increased speculation surrounding his next move, with Madrid retaining a significant advantage over other potential suitors.

Paz left Madrid for Como in the summer of 2024, having made only eight senior appearances for the Spanish giants.

His move to Italy initially offered an opportunity to gain regular first-team experience, but the relationship between the two clubs has since become more complicated.

During the summer of 2026, Como reportedly paid an additional €60m to acquire full ownership of the player, while Madrid retained a final buy-back option worth €80m.

That clause is valid for the summer of 2027, meaning Madrid have a limited opportunity to bring their former academy player back on preferential terms.

COPE now reports that the Spanish giants intend to exercise that option, although the deal has not been officially completed.

As previously reported by Sports Mole, Madrid face an important decision over Paz's future, particularly because of the attacking competition awaiting him at the Bernabeu.

Bellingham has established himself as a key figure in Madrid's midfield, while Guler has also become increasingly influential under Jose Mourinho.

The club possesses several other attacking options, including Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Yan Diomande. Consequently, there is no guarantee that Paz would enjoy the same importance in Madrid's starting XI that he currently possesses at Como.

Veron's comments about another young Argentine, Franco Mastantuono, offer an interesting perspective on that challenge.

Discussing the youngster's development during his loan spell at Fiorentina, Veron argued that consistent opportunities were essential for establishing himself at the highest level.

"Nico Paz became a leader at Como by playing," he explained. "I have never known a player who became a team leader by sitting on the bench."

Veron was discussing the benefits of regular football rather than explicitly warning Paz against returning to Madrid. Nevertheless, his observations underline an important consideration for the Spanish club as it weighs up the midfielder's future.

Paz reportedly chose to remain at Como last summer because he wanted to continue developing through regular appearances, and his decision has been rewarded by an outstanding start to the new campaign.

Manchester United have also been linked with the Argentina international, although Madrid's contractual advantage places the Spanish giants in a stronger position.

For Los Blancos, securing a player whose value has risen considerably could represent an attractive investment. For Paz, the sporting challenge would be to turn the promise recognised by Veron into an influential role at a club where competition for attacking positions is already fierce.

Marseille welcome Le Mans to the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening for round 11 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.

Since their narrow 2-1 loss to back-to-back European champions Paris Saint-Germain on September 20, Les Olympiens have been an unstoppable force, winning each of their previous five domestic matches to rise to fourth in the Ligue 1 table and sit just five points off Les Parisiens at the summit.

The biggest strength of Bruno Genesio’s side has undoubtedly been their free flowing attack, as after 10 league games, Marseille have netted an impressive 22 goals, a tally that cannot be bettered by any other side in the division.

However, Les Olympiens will undoubtedly be disappointed with their performances in the UEFA Europa League, as after four league phase fixtures they have picked up just three points and currently reside outside of the tournament’s progression places to the knockout stage.

Having gone unbeaten in each of their previous six encounters with Le Mans, including a 2-1 victory in their most recent meeting at the Stade Velodrome in January 2010, Marseille will be confident that they can continue their fine league form this weekend though and mount a charge towards PSG in top spot.

After ending their 16-year wait for promotion to France’s top tier at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, beating Bastia 2-0 away from home on the final day to pip St. Etienne to second place, Le Mans will have mixed feelings about their start to life in Ligue 1 this season.

Although they lost just one of their opening five Ligue 1 matches to start the campaign, Patrick Videira’s men have failed to claim a league victory in over two months, leaving them 15th in the table with eight points and only outside of the relegation places on goal difference.

Without a doubt, Les Manceaux’s weakness in the 2026-27 season has been their leaky defence, as Sunday’s visitors have conceded a concerning 19 league goals so far and are one of three sides alongside Lens and Strasbourg that are yet to keep a clean sheet.

Despite previously claiming victory at the Stade Velodrome, posting a famous 3-2 win in September 1994, Le Mans head into Sunday’s match in poor form, facing Marseille as massive underdogs, and knowing they’ll need to pull off another monumental triumph if they want to get their season back on track this weekend.

Marseille are still without Italian full-back Emerson Palmieri, who is expected to return before the end of the year from a knee issue, while Canadian midfielder Derek Cornelius continues his struggles with a hip problem.

On a more positive note, Genesio will be glad that a cohort of important first team players including the likes of Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Nayef Aguerd and Geoffrey Kondogbia have all returned from the international break unscathed.

Netting an impressive seven Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous three league outings, Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly Les Olympiens’ dangerman and will be hoping to close the gap to Paris FC’s Lassine Sinayoko at the top of the division’s scoring charts on Sunday evening.

Le Mans are certain to be missing Algerian midfielder Adil Bourabaa and former Everton defender Djibril Sidibe this weekend as the pair are ruled out with ankle and foot injuries respectively.

It remains to be seen whether either Samuel Yohou, who has reportedly sustained a head injury, or young French midfielder Martin Rossignol can fight off issues to feature at the Stade Velodrome too.

After signing from Ligue 2 side Guingamp in the summer, 32-year-old striker Louis Mafouta has been the visitors’ biggest attacking threat this season, scoring a respectable four goals in 10 league matches.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Hojbjerg, Nnadi; Harit, Abdelli, Paixao; Gouiri

Kocik; Bamba, Torrente, Voyer; Vercruysse; Buades, Traore, Bretelle, Calodat; Mafouta, Gueye

Having emphatically bounced back from their early season woes, Marseille will be confident that they can beat any opponent they come up against and continue their impressive rise up the table.

Although Le Mans will be desperate to turn around their poor form, we believe the hosts will be far too strong and are backing them to close the gap on the teams above by posting a convincing victory at the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening.

#1544. I can understand why fans are frustrated about lack of progress under Pocognoli, admits Andy Robertson

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026

Andy Robertson says he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Monday’s heavy defeat to Switzerland marked the conclusion of a dismal Nations League campaign which saw the Belgian’s men beat only North Macedonia across six matches to finish a distant third.

After the high of qualifying for the World Cup a year ago, supporters have been brought crashing back to earth since the summer with signs of progress proving hard to come by under the new manager.

When the full-time whistle blew in St Gallen to confirm a 4-0 loss, there were audible jeers from the travelling fans.

Skipper Robertson has no issue with what he heard and knows the players have a job on their hands to turn the situation round.

‘I can understand why they’re concerned. I can understand why they’re frustrated,’ he said. ‘I can understand why the away fans didn’t really want us to go over and applaud them.

Robertson can't hide anguish after 4-0 loss on what was his record breaking 103rd cap

‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate new people into a new squad and things like that.

‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team

‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he said. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the new players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he said. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11  players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland

‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’

Juventus have tied academy forward Destiny Elimoghale to the club until 30 June 2029, on the day Giovanni Carnevali spoke to shareholders about the youth sector. The 2009-born striker has already been named in a European squad while injuries stretch the first team.

He was among Massimo Brambilla’s unused substitutes in the 1-1 home draw with Pro Vercelli on 2 November. That matchday 12 fixture was the Next Gen’s most recent game.

Carnevali confirmed a change to the UEFA squad list as well, with Ekhator replacing Locatelli.

#1542. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

The assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

#1540. Sassuolo vs. Genoa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 21:13

Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.

The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.

Sassuolo's brief association with Alberto Aquilani lasted just 11 league matches, with the board in Reggio Emilia making another managerial change to arrest the club's poor run of results.

Admittedly, the Black and Greens made a respectable start under the former midfielder, collecting seven points from their opening four games as a three-match unbeaten run followed an opening-day 2-1 defeat at Atalanta BC.

However, mid-September's 2-1 reverse at Monza began a seven-match winless league sequence, and Sassuolo's defensive record under Aquilani made for grim reading.

The Neroverdi conceded a staggering 19 goals across five defeats, losing 4-2 to Frosinone, 2-0 to Como, 6-2 to Lazio, 4-2 to Fiorentina and 3-0 at Roma.

The defeat at the Olimpico proved the final straw for the 17th-placed outfit, who sit just one point clear of the relegation zone and two ahead of 19th-placed Venezia.

That underlines the scale of the task facing D'Aversa, who inherits a side that have conceded 29 Serie A goals, four more than both Monza and bottom-placed Udinese, two of the teams currently occupying the relegation places.

Daniele De Rossi's men will hope that the new boss needs time to adapt to his surroundings as they seek to extend the Black and Greens' losing sequence.

The travelling supporters will welcome this weekend's trip, given that the Grifone have claimed four consecutive victories in this fixture, including two at Mapei Stadium.

Beyond those recent successes in Reggio Emilia, the Ligurian outfit enter this weekend as one of the competition's form teams.

Their 2-1 home defeat to AC Milan before the international break ended Genoa's three-match winning streak, during which they stunned Juventus 2-0 in front of their supporters.

Having collected 12 points from their last 18 in Serie A, losing to Roma and Milan during that improved run, De Rossi's men will back themselves to overcome any new-manager bounce in Emilia-Romagna and claim consecutive away league victories for the first time since November-December 2024, when they beat Parma 1-0 and Udinese 2-0.

D'Aversa has several fitness concerns ahead of his first Sassuolo match: Cristian Volpato, Yeferson Paz, Daniel Boloca, Domenico Berardi and Vasilije Adzic will be assessed before Sunday's clash; however, Fedde Leysen (knee) and Ismael Kone (broken leg) are sidelined.

If three-goal Adzic cannot feature, the new manager will have to rely on Sebastiano Esposito and Armand Lauriente, who have scored twice apiece, to shoulder more of the Black and Greens' attacking burden.

Genoa, meanwhile, will look to Milutin Osmajic and Junior Messias to add to their respective Serie A tallies of four and two goals, while Stephan El Shaarawy has registered two assists in his last three appearances for the Ligurian outfit.

A relatively healthy squad further boosts the visitors' prospects, although Morten Frendrup remains doubtful due to the ankle problem that kept him out of the Rossoblu's defeat to Milan last time out.

Muric; Walukiewicz, Caleta-Car, Idzes, Doig; Thorstvedt, Matic, Sulemana; Dominguez, Lauriente; Esposito

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Wiafe, Traore, Ellertsson; Junior Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic

Sassuolo's injury doubts complicate D'Aversa's first assignment, particularly with Berardi and Adzic potentially unavailable to bolster an attack already struggling to compensate for the team's defensive frailties.

Genoa arrive with fewer fitness concerns and a confident Osmajic, suggesting that De Rossi's men can secure a fifth successive victory over the Neroverdi.

Juventus won 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar on a night when Teun Koopmeiners faced his old club, even though the hosts dominated the expected-goals count. The result strengthens their league-phase position ahead of Sunday's Serie A trip to Fiorentina.

“I love Endrick, and Real Madrid are more important than him. We need Endrick here and Real Madrid coach needs Endrick here,” he began.

“This is the answer to those who write things and agents. Then if the club decides other things, I respect that. But for me, as Real Madrid coach, Endrick is important. I need him.”

The ‘agents’ that Mourinho is referring to could well be Endrick’s entourage, who have given comments suggesting that a move is being explored, while they reportedly visited Milano in recent days too.

#1536. Konyaspor vs Besiktas - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:40, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:42

Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.

Konyaspor have endured a difficult run of results in recent weeks, winning just once in their last six league matches and struggling to find consistency in the final third.

Ilhan Palut's side began that sequence with consecutive goalless draws against Kasimpasa and Istanbul Basaksehir before suffering a 1-0 defeat away to Amed SK.

They then recorded a 2-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi, but that proved to be their only success during the period as they suffered consecutive defeats against Galatasaray (4-0) and Samsunspor (1-0).

Konyaspor were particularly disappointing in their defeat away to Samsunspor just before the break, failing to take anything from a match against a side sitting second-bottom and enduring a losing run.

The result further highlighted their struggles in front of goal, with the hosts having scored just six times in their opening 11 league matches, an average of fewer than one per game, while they have failed to find the net in seven of those fixtures.

Konyaspor have scored four of their six goals and collected seven of their eight points on home soil, although they were thrashed by Galatasaray in their last home game and now face a Besiktas side that have beaten them in their last two league meetings.

The hosts did manage to defeat the Black Eagles 1-0 in their most recent encounter, although that victory came in the Turkish Cup.

Besiktas, meanwhile, have enjoyed a more productive campaign, collecting seven wins, one draw and three defeats from their opening 11 league matches to remain within reach of the leading teams, sitting six points behind league leaders Galatasaray.

Vincenzo Italiano's side are also unbeaten in their last three league games, a sequence that began with a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir before they were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa.

Their subsequent European fixture saw them suffer a 3-2 defeat against Celtic, but they responded positively three days later by recording a convincing 3-0 home win over Genclerbirligi.

Dusan Vlahovic was particularly influential in that victory, scoring twice as the Black Eagles returned to winning ways in the Super Lig and demonstrated the attacking quality that has made them one of the more productive sides in the division, with only four teams scoring more than their 23 goals.

However, the visitors have struggled on the road, winning just one of their five away league matches and failing to win any of their last three, during which they have recorded one draw and two defeats.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from a cruciate ligament injury and is expected to remain sidelined for the rest of the season.

Chidozie Awaziem is also unlikely to feature after sustaining a muscle injury, while Marko Jevtovic is working towards regaining full fitness and faces a late assessment.

Ugurcan Yazgili is another concern after picking up a hamstring problem, leaving Palut with defensive and midfield decisions to make.

Mostafa Mohamed, Diogo Goncalves and Ebrima Colley are among the attacking options available to the Konyaspor manager, although Enis Bardhi is expected to miss out through suspension.

Besiktas will be without Umit Akdag, who is recovering from a broken wrist, while Fabio Miretti is also expected to miss the match with a shoulder injury.

Emmanuel Agbadou is not expected to return until later in December as he continues his recovery from a knee problem, while Orkun Kokcu is also sidelined with a foot injury.

Gungordu; Andzouana, Baniya, Bosluk, Masuaku; Toth, Ibrahimoglu; Colley, Goncalves, Dompe; Mohamed

Nubel; Murillo, Taylan Bulut, Topcu, R Yilmaz; Ndidi; Trossard, S Ozcan, Olaitan, Fakili; Vlahovic

Konyaspor have struggled to produce consistent attacking performances this season, and although Besiktas have been inconsistent on the road, their attacking quality should be enough to overcome the hosts' defensive resistance, with Italiano's side expected to secure a comfortable victory in Konya.

#1535. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. As the strains of We’ll Live and Die in These Towns dies down to segue into the Eton Boating Song, Newcastle kick off, attacking from right to left. When they lose the ball Wissa is penalised for tripping Rudoni 45 yards out.

Coventry are in blue and white stripes, harking back to the 1987 Cup final rather than the Mick Coop years. Newcastle are in vibrant lilac.

It was good to get a win. We worked very hard for it. It’s so hard to get wins, especially on the road. And now we’re back at home and we have to work on those attributes [that earned us the win] at Forest. We rotated pretty well, there are different aspects of the game we want to improve on regardless of shape.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1530. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli not feeling the heat after dismal Nations League campaign

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:40 EST, 17 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli insists he’s unconcerned about calls for his head after a dismal start to his time in charge of Scotland.

Monday’s 4-0 defeat to Switzerland confirmed that the Belgian’s side finished a distant third in their Nations League section with the only two wins in six games coming against North Macedonia.

After a decent start to the match in St Gallen, Scotland fell behind to a Lewis Ferguson own goal and the result was put beyond doubt when the Swiss scored two quick goals at the outset of the second half.

With another performance falling way short of expectations and little sign of progress, the new manager is increasingly coming under pressure.

Despite only being in charge for 13 weeks, pundits including Michael Stewart have already called on the Scottish Football Association to draw a line under Pocognoli’s reign.

Adamant that he’s not feeling the heat, though, the 39-year-old insisted: ‘I am not thinking about this. I am just looking ahead to the next camp in March and the start of the qualification.

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is confident he'll get Scotland back on track

Skipper Andy Robertson reacts at full-time to the 4-0 defeat against Switzerland

‘We have to take the most we can from the last two camps and try to build something strong for the next one. The objective is to reach the Euros in the best position possible.

‘We will have ups and downs and it was not good in terms of the score against Switzerland. But, for me as a coach, it was a good game to see us against a strong nation away from home. That’s something we have to take into the future.’

Asked how he dealt with the growing clamour for his dismissal, he replied: ‘I don’t accept this to be honest. It’s always like this when you have a bad moment, when you think about the past. But always thinking about the past is an energy taker — we have to look forward.’

The successor to Steve Clarke, Pocognoli has tried to bring in a more attacking philosophy via a 3-4-2-1 formation.

While his reluctance to adapt has also drawn widespread criticism, he claims he’s not averse to coming up with a different approach.

‘It’s possible,’ he added. ‘I did it in Monaco and we won many tough games with a back four. I also won many good games with a back three.

‘We played in the Champions League and in half of the games we played with a different shape, so it doesn’t mean that I’m not flexible. But the timeline is to do what we are trying to do now.’

Asked if the job was proving to be tougher than he anticipated, Pocognoli said: ‘No. I think we nearly had a good game. It was just the score and the aspects in the boxes. That’s where there’s disappointment.

‘It’s step by step. And we have created a lot of chances in four of the six games. And in these six games we played one of them with 10 men and another where we were not on the level at all against Slovenia.’

Goztepe could be without Furkan Bayir and Ogun Bayrak, who have both been reported as injury doubts, while Ibrahim Sabra is continuing his recovery from an ankle injury after returning to training.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

The hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

Referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

#1525. Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies: Who has won more honours?

By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32

Liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies count 69-68 on every senior competitive honour as of November 20, 2026.

With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.

Neither club has lifted a trophy since Liverpool's 2024-25 Premier League title, which nudged the Anfield outfit back ahead of their eternal rivals.

Liverpool and Manchester United share the record for English league titles with 20 each, after the Merseysiders' 2024-25 Premier League win matched the total the Red Devils reached in 2012-13.

United are stronger in the FA Cup, with 13 wins to Liverpool's eight, and in the Community Shield, which they have won or shared 21 times against 16 for the Anfield club.

Liverpool hold the record of 10 League Cups, four more than their rivals, and they are the only one of the pair to have won the Football League Super Cup, which was played only once.

The gap opens up in Europe, where six European Cups, three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups give the Reds 13 continental trophies to United's six.

Liverpool have more trophies than Manchester United on the fullest count, one ahead, and they also lead when Community Shields are left out.

United only draw level if the 1986 Football League Super Cup is removed or shared Community Shields are discounted, and they only go ahead on a count limited to the league, FA Cup and League Cup, which they lead 39-38.

That makes the Reds the more decorated club, since they lead or are level on every method that includes European competition, and the only count that favours the Old Trafford side ignores continental silverware altogether.

United's honours board leaves out the Super Cup and so shows the rivals level, which is a fair reading, but even on that basis the Red Devils still need one more trophy to go ahead.

Opinion is split on whether the Community Shield should count as a genuine trophy, and the FA itself treats it as a friendly for disciplinary purposes, so bookings in it do not carry over into other domestic games.

The fixture has only been contested between the league champions and the FA Cup winners since 1974, and before that it was an invitational match.

Seven of United's Community Shields and three of Liverpool's came before that change, which strengthens the case for leaving the trophy out.

The Anfield club's own honours page lists 52 major men's honours, a figure that excludes both the Community Shield and the Football League Super Cup, and the Community Shield never appeared on the honours board at their old Melwood training ground either.

Counting the Football League Super Cup but not the Community Shield gives the Reds a 53-47 lead, a six-trophy cushion over the Red Devils.

The Football League Super Cup was set up after the Heysel Stadium disaster in May 1985 and the European ban on English clubs that followed, as a replacement competition for the six sides who would have played on the continent in 1985-86.

Liverpool beat Everton in a two-legged final held back until September 1986, winning 3-1 at Anfield and 4-1 at Goodison Park for a 7-2 aggregate victory.

The tournament was never played again, which is why some honours boards ignore it, and counting it or not decides whether the Merseysiders lead or the clubs are level.

A drawn Community Shield used to be shared, and Liverpool's list includes five shared editions (1964, 1965, 1977, 1986 and 1990), while United shared four (1965, 1967, 1977 and 1990).

The years 1965, 1977 and 1990 appear on both lists, and removing every shared Community Shield leaves both clubs on 64, another count where Man United can claim a tie but not a lead.

Manchester United have their strongest case at home, with 60 domestic honours to Liverpool's 55 when Community Shields and the Football League Super Cup are counted.

In the three main domestic competitions, the league, FA Cup and League Cup, the Red Devils lead 39-38 thanks to five more FA Cup wins.

Cup finals between the pair have been split evenly, as United won the 1977 FA Cup final 2-1 and the 1996 final 1-0, while the Reds won the League Cup finals of 1983 and 2003.

The 1983 final went to extra time, with Alan Kennedy and Ronnie Whelan cancelling out Norman Whiteside's opener for a 2-1 win, and Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen scored in the 2-0 win in Cardiff 20 years later.

For every result between the two clubs rather than just the silverware, our Man Utd vs. Liverpool head-to-head record covers each meeting.

Liverpool's six European Cups are more than any other British team has won and double United's three, and that record is what separates the clubs.

The Reds add three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups, while United's six European trophies are completed by a Europa League, a Cup Winners' Cup and one UEFA Super Cup.

United edge the world honours 2-1, having won the 1999 Intercontinental Cup and the 2008 Club World Cup, while the Merseysiders won the Club World Cup in 2019.

For the stories behind several of those European nights, including the 2005 final in Istanbul, our rundown of Liverpool's 10 greatest comebacks goes back through the club's most dramatic recoveries.

Manchester United's modern haul was built under Sir Alex Ferguson, who won 38 trophies in 26 years in charge between 1986 and 2013, including 13 league titles, five FA Cups and two Champions League titles.

The teams behind that run feature heavily in our ranking of Manchester United's 10 greatest ever teams, which sets the Ferguson sides against the club's earlier eras.

The latest swings came in 2023-24, when Liverpool's League Cup win put them one ahead on the full count before the Red Devils beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final to draw level again.

The Reds' 2024-25 Premier League title then put them one clear, while on the count that ignores the Super Cup the same sequence went from a tie to a United lead and back to the current tie.

Liverpool and Manchester United are both in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase, so Europe offers the biggest single swing, alongside the FA Cup, the League Cup and the next Community Shield.

One trophy for United without a reply from Anfield would level the full count, while any Liverpool success would stretch the gap to two.

Liverpool appear to have a better chance of adding to their haul in the 2026-27 campaign, with Man United out of the League Cup and having seen any faint hopes of a title challenge evaporate amidst their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

The Old Trafford side are now led by Mauricio Pochettino, who became head coach in November 2026 after Michael Carrick was sacked.

To see what the new head coach brings, our breakdown of Pochettino's record against every Premier League club shows how his past teams have fared against each top-flight side.

For a view of current strength rather than history, our ranking of the best football teams in the world shows where Liverpool sit among Europe's elite.

#1524. GdS: ‘Old to who?’ – Modric chasing Milan record while future remains unwritten

Luka Modric may be 41 years of age, but he shows no signs of slowing down. In fact, he remains crucial or both AC Milan and Croatia.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by pointing out that Sunday’s game will be a first for Modric, even given the hundreds of games he has played. The midfielder will face Frosinone for the first time, the 227th opponent of his long career (155 at club level and 72 for the national team).

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In ten days, Modric will have gone from from London’s Wembley Stadium where he faced England, to the Opus Arena in Osijek, Croatia, where he beat the Czech Republic and played 90 minutes as captain, back to San Siro for the Frosinone game.

Yesterday, Luka returned to Milanello and trained with the Rossoneri, ready to take charge of the group again when the tournament resumes. He’s one of the eight players in the squad who have surpassed 800 minutes of total playing time across all competitions, including goalkeepers.

The Ballon d’Or winner has featured 13 times this season, with 11 being in the league (eight starts), and twice as a substitute in the Europa League. For his national team, he’s appeared in six Nations League matches, four of them from the start.

The match against Spain on October 6th was supposed to be his farewell to Croatia, but instead he was easily persuaded to stay and continue. He’s played 19 of the 21 matches since August, accumulating over a thousand minutes – 1,114 to be precise.

Modric scored for Milan at 40 years, five months and four days (the winner against Pisa) and is third in the ranking of the oldest goal scorers in the club’s history. Alessandro Costacurta is second (41 years, 25 days) and Zlatan Ibrahimovic is first (41 years, 5 months, and 15 days).

So, another record is in sight in the present, but what about the future? Modric is tied to Milan until the summer, with his contract expiring in June 2027. There are no further options for an extension but the relationship between player and club goes beyond written agreements.

Luka will decide his own future, as he did last summer, choosing to stay. He still wanted Milan despite being left behind without his family (who had since returned to Madrid) out of love for the Rossoneri. Next season, who knows?

#1523. Juventus Next Gen beaten 4-0 at Lecco and left third from bottom

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

The opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

The hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He said his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

The table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s plans.

One player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His new contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

Elimoghale was called up to the first-team squad for the first time on 17 September 2026. That call-up came for the opening Europa League league-phase match against NEC.

The next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

The next test comes quickly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

Chelsea star Pedro Neto lost his cool while playing for Portugal in their win over Wales as he received two yellow cards in as many minutes before clashing with opposing manager Craig Bellamy.

The Blues winger had in fact scored in the game, netting his side's second goal at the Cardiff City Stadium, but saw his game fall apart in the second-half.

He was first booked for a high challenge on the back of Brennan Johnson's leg – a tackle which some may argue could have been a red in itself.

One minute and 59 seconds later, he was shown his second yellow when he slid in on Johnson again. He didn't appear to make too much contact, if any, but left the Wales man sprawling to avoid it.

German referee Sven Jablonski showed no hesitation in sending Neto off, but the winger wasn't going to take it lying down.

He had to be held back by captain Bruno Fernandes as he tried to confront Johnson, and seemingly managed to shout in his direction before reluctantly making his way off the field.

Pedro Neto was sent off while playing for Portugal against Wales after two yellow cards in under two minutes

He also had a confrontation with Wales manager Craig Bellamy (right) as he left the field of play

Before that, though, he had a conversation with Wales boss Craig Bellamy, with officials initially trying to separate the two, with Neto looking angry.

Bellamy, though, spoke to Neto and embraced him before finally walking down the tunnel.

The 26-year-old will now serve a one-game suspension, meaning he will miss the first leg of Portugal's Nations League quarter-final, which will be played in March.

Jorge Jesus's side secured top spot in their group with the win over Wales, which was achieved by Carlos Forbs's 70th-minute goal.

Fernandes had opened the scoring for his side in the 11th minute, but David Brooks and Sorba Thomas gave Wales an unlikely lead.

That was until Neto levelled things up just before half-time, and Forbs scored the winner, with ten-man Portugal able to hold on for all three points.

Wales finished bottom of the group with one win – against Norway – and five defeats from their six matches.

Captain Ben Davies said after the game: 'We showed a lot of character and we've shown good effort in these games where we've just come up short from a results perspective.

After expressing his frustration, the Chelsea star had to be directed off the field by captain Bruno Fernandes (right)

He had in fact scored for his side in the game, bringing them level before the half-time interval

'There is a lot to take from this going into the games in March and we have to feel confident because we've been playing well.

'We know the boys up top can be so dangerous, and if teams want to come here and play man-for-man against us, we've got a lot of speed and we have to be good on the ball. That comes with risk sometimes, like you saw with the chances that they had, but I'd rather play this way and go toe-to-toe with these teams and have a go.

'We competed in the campaign and we were not a million miles off like the table might suggest. I thought we put in some very good performances, we just wished we had some better results.'

Neto, meanwhile, will now return to his club side Chelsea ahead of a busy Christmas period.

He has started all but one Premier League game so far and has been a key player under new manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues will take on Leeds at Stamford Bridge this weekend as club football returns.

#1521. Virgil van Dijk contract latest: Liverpool captain makes "no idea" admission ahead of milestone appearance in Man United clash

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:10

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a new Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk said.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he has had to settle for seven wins in his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

#1520. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.
