#1488. McKennie says USA players could follow Pochettino to Manchester United

Weston McKennie has said USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there. Juventus, already without Thuram and Locatelli, now face pressure to rule out a mid-season sale.

The question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford. His answer was that it could potentially happen.

McKennie called the speculation inevitable. He said many USA players are due to change clubs within the next year, calciomercato.com reported.

Pochettino was asked about the same subject. He said now was not the right time to discuss it. He added that United are among the very top clubs and a dream for many players.

Pochettino and his staff remain in charge of the USA for two games against Haiti, on 14 and 17 November. United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

The comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s plans and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

His contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

McKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

The club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

The timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Thuram is out until 2027 after knee surgery. Captain Manuel Locatelli also faces a long absence after twisting his right knee against Milan. He had surgery in Lyon on 8 September to repair the external meniscus, and Corriere dello Sport put his lay-off at five to six months.

Losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He said nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

The next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

#1487. PSG: Ferran Torres, a shortage which is seriously starting to worry

There are evenings which only accentuate doubts. The one experienced by Ferran Torres against Troyes on Saturday evening is undoubtedly one of them. In a meeting where Paris Saint-Germain ended up finding the fault to win (1-0), the Spanish striker, aligned in a right winger role, once again went through the debates without managing to be sufficiently decisive. However, there was no shortage of opportunities and opportunities to find the net presented themselves to him. But as too often in recent weeks, the last gesture was lacking. A new frustrating performance which extends a worrying period of scarcity for a player whose offensive efficiency is nevertheless one of the main missions.

The Trojan evening did not allow Ferran Torres to smile again. From the 38th minute of play, the Spaniard came up against Hillel Konaté in a tight angle, before missing two new opportunities just before the break, in the 45th and 45th+2. In the second half, the scenario repeated itself: served by Fabián Ruiz in the 67th minute, he again saw the Trojan goalkeeper reject his attempt. Four clear chances, four failures and an exit in the 70th minute, replaced by Quentin Ndjantou. The contrast is striking with his Parisian debut: after scoring seven goals in his first six appearances, Torres is now going through a series of eight games without scoring.

As a reminder, his last goal dates back to September 20, during the victory against Olympique de Marseille in Ligue 1. In the Champions League, he has not found the net since his hat-trick against Slovan Bratislava. Faced with growing questions, Luis Enrique however chose to defend his attacker. Asked at a press conference about his difficulties, the Parisian coach, in fact, wanted to put this less good period into perspective: “everyone was concerned about Mika Godts, now it’s Ferran. These are attackers who miss and score goals.. A protective speech which reflects the technician’s desire not to publicly overwhelm his player.

In the mixed zone, Lucas Beraldo also recalled the importance of solidarity within the Parisian locker room, without wanting to dwell on the individual case of his teammate. “Torres? As I said, every match is different, tonight we played against a very good team, we managed to score and win and that’s the most important thing. At PSG, we are a family, in good times and in bad times.. Valuable support for the Spaniard, who will now have to quickly regain his effectiveness. Because if Luis Enrique continues to place his trust in him, the missed opportunities begin to accumulate and the shortage becomes difficult to ignore.

#1486. GdS: Krösche announcement could come next week – how he will operate at Milan

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s plans.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

“Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche said upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

A trip far from trivial. Philippe Diallo knows it, the African continent constitutes particularly favorable terrain for Gianni Infantino. The outgoing president benefits from significant support, which his opponent intends to try to change. But this strategy is far from unanimous. The independent journalist, although an opponent of Gianni Infantino, does not mince his words. Romain Molina denounces in particular a lack of understanding of the balance of power within international bodies and African federations. #1484. Juventus sell out Venezia game as Omonia sales pass 35,000

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

General sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

This season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

The Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

#1483. You're Not Nineteenth Forever! Sacked Man United manager Michael Carrick looks relieved to be out of the relegation fight as he watches The Courteeners at gig in London

Published: 04:29 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 18 November 2026

Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.

Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.

That came despite his incredible impact in the second half of last season when he replaced Ruben Amorim and led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League.

And on Saturday night, a few days after his tenure ended, Carrick attended a tour date of The Courteeners.

According to the band's schedule, they were performing at Alexandra Palace in London.

One fan shared a photo on X from the gig, with the caption 'One hell of a day out'.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend (Source X/adamkearey)

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

Some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

Following his sacking on Thursday after ten months in charge, Carrick issued a heartfelt statement reflecting on his tenure.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’

Carrick was relieved of his duties at Man United on Thursday after a dismal start to the season

The axe ultimately fell on Carrick on Thursday, yet the writing was on the wall for several days beforehand as speculation spread and United's hierarchy worked towards an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino.

Many former United stars were hugely critical of their former club, with Gary Neville calling their treatment of Carrick 'disgusting', while Peter Schmeichel labelled it 'very disrespectful'.

Rio Ferdinand also compared United's 142-word statement announcing his sacking to 'like ChatGPT' after there was no comment added by club chiefs.

United are back in action on Sunday when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool in what will be Pochettino's first game in charge.

#1482. Harry Kane: “I have always been a big admirer of Karim Benzema”

French Football Weekly: entering the very closed circle of Ballon d’Or winners allowed you to feel fully established among the greatest strikers of all time? Do we need to win this trophy to have the recognition we deserve in the world of football?

Harry Kane: I am extremely proud to have won the Ballon d’Or, and receiving this award in my hometown made the moment even more special. Seeing my name alongside players like R9, who actually gave it to me that evening, Cristiano Ronaldo, Messi and Gerd Müller is an immense source of pride, especially given my journey with loans at the start of my career which forced me to show self-confidence and resilience. Since arriving at Bayern, I have clearly taken a new step, and I feel like I am at the top of my game. I think winning the Ballon d’Or has changed the way people perceive me around the world. I probably underestimated the enthusiasm and the reaction of the fans. When I brandished the trophy in front of the supporters who were waiting for me in the street as I left the ceremony, I understood that I was experiencing a magical moment that I will never forget. This victory is the reflection of an exceptional season that I experienced between the goals, the titles and the great moments. Winning the Ballon d’Or at 33 just shows that if you continue to work hard and believe in it, you can reach the top.

FM: Karim Benzema was Ballon d’Or in 2022, Harry Kane was Ballon d’Or in 2026. The full number 9s who participate in the game are highlighted. Do you find any similarities between you and Karim Benzema in your football?

HK: Karim is an incredible player. I have always been a big admirer of the player. What he achieved at Real Madrid in 2022 was truly impressive. He has this ability to drop into midfield and play almost like a number 10, dictating the play, while arriving in the box at the ideal time. We have slightly different physical characteristics, but in terms of playing intelligence, ability to find spaces and desire to help the players around us, I clearly see a lot of similarities in our football. Both of us showed that it is not always necessary to be in the box to score goals. For me, I have more opportunities when I go lower, because I’m not marked up close. The goals come from me going down and the game developing. I find myself in a number 10 role and, when the opposing block moves back, I shoot from the edge of the area, which is one of my great assets. Last season was the best example: I scored 73 goals, which is almost double the number of goals I scored in any other season.

FM: after winning a Ballon d’Or, what is the priority objective? Go get a second one to make even more history?

HK: of course, I would love to win another Ballon d’Or, but I know there are many other great players who have their chances. But there are still many trophies I would like to win, like the Champions League with Bayern and, obviously, a title with England.

FM: Last year, your journey in the Champions League ended in the semi-final against PSG after a very high-level double confrontation. Do you think that, this season, Bayern Munich is capable of going for the big-eared cup?

HK: the Champions League is a major goal for me and for the team. We have a strong squad, made up of incredible players. Last season, the matches against PSG were crazy, it was decided by a hair, and being eliminated by the team which won the title twice in a row was nothing to be ashamed of. Spending another year with the coach and the team helps us become even stronger. We approached this season telling ourselves that this had to be our year. We have to find a way to achieve this, find that little extra that will make the difference to get through the rounds and do everything we can to win the Champions League. This is our main objective.

FM: You are the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d’Or in over 45 years. Can a player like Michael Olise be your successor, the next Munich player to win this Grail?

HK: Michael is a fantastic player. We see, every day in training, his qualities and what he is capable of doing on the pitch. He undoubtedly has the means to bring a new Ballon d’Or to Munich, that’s for sure.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Liverpool enjoying all of the possession so far, LASK are defending in a 5-2-3 shape, so Liverpool’s full-backs should have some time and space. Gravenberch does well to win a foul in midfield.

The home team play in all red, so Liverpool are in their white away strip. It looks like there is some Liverpool support among the locals/neutrals in the home end.

LASK XI: Jungwirth, Jorgensen, Mbuyamba, Alemao, Andrade, Dibango, Danek, Bogarde, Schopf, Lang, Adeniran

Subs: Schutzenauer, Schillinger, Freckleton, Ljubicic, Kalajdzic, Verhaeghe, Elfadli, Flecker, Kane.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

One novice who certainly deserves his starting spot is Trey Nyoni, the England Under-21 international has impressed in the opportunities he has been given so far this year. Watch out for his calmness on the ball and the efficiency with which he uses it.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola said: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

“They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”

24 - Liverpool's starting XI against LASK has an average age of 24 years and 186 days, their third-youngest ever for a UEFA Champions League game, older only than September 2001 v Borussia Dortmund (24y 136d) and December 2020 v Midtjylland (24y 26d). Knocks. https://t.co/4JeW73N87k

Iraola makes four changes from the defeat by City so in come Frimpong, Tsimikas, Nyoni and Ngumoha.

Liverpool XI: Alisson, Frimpong, Araujo, Jacquet, Tsimikas, Nyoni, Gravenberch, Wirtz, Barcola, Koumas, Ngumoha

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Munoz, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Sonni-Lambie, Lucky

Our team to take on LASK ✊ #UCL https://t.co/8vObg7mgLF

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1479. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

#1478. AC Milan targets €60m striker

AC Milan would have found its priority to strengthen its attack during the next winter transfer window. According to information from La Gazzetta dello Sportthe Rossoneri leaders have made Nicolò Tresoldi their main target and are ready to negotiate a transfer estimated at 60 million euros with Club Bruges. At just 22 years old, the German striker has had an excellent start to the season in Belgium, with 14 goals scored for club, including eight in the league, five in the Champions League and one in the Belgian Super Cup. He also has four goals with the German Espoirs. Performances which convinced Milan to favor his profile over that of Endrick, also followed in recent months. The young center forward knows San Siro perfectly, where he scored a hat-trick against the Milanese in the Champions League last October. A supporter of the Italian club since childhood, Tresoldi would be particularly enthusiastic about joining the Rossoneri. His family and representatives would also welcome a transfer to Serie A, an element likely to facilitate discussions between the two teams.

But to complete this operation, AC Milan will have to convince Club Bruges, who would not wish to part with their striker for less than 60 million euros. A substantial amount that Gerry Cardinale, owner of the Lombard club, would be willing to negotiate personally. The two clubs already have relations on the transfer market, notably after the operations concerning Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari. Milan wants to accelerate from January, even if an agreement could be postponed until next summer. The recruitment of a new center forward has become a priority due to the offensive performance considered insufficient by the current squad. Gonçalo Ramos has only scored three goals in all competitions, while Francesco Camarda has yet to find the net. The latter could also be loaned in order to benefit from more playing time. At the same time, the Endrick track seems to be fading away, the Brazilian having recently reaffirmed his attachment to Real Madrid and his wish to continue his career there. The Italian club is now focusing its efforts on Tresoldi, with the ambition of quickly strengthening its offensive sector to achieve its objectives in the league and return to the Champions League.

#1476. Juan Mata retires aged 38: Premier League legend calls time on glittering career as Manchester United pay tribute to former star

Published: 05:52 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 05:53 EST, 18 November 2026

Former Manchester United and Chelsea star Juan Mata has retired from football at the age of 38.

The Spain star, who came through Real Madrid's academy before winning the Champions League with Chelsea and the Europa League with both the Blues and Man United, enjoyed a dazzling career in England before moving to clubs in Turkey, Japan and Australia.

The midfielder also distinguished himself for his national side, winning the 2010 World Cup as part of the squad, and scoring in Spain's victorious Euro 2012 final against Italy.

Most recently featuring in Australia's A-League for Melbourne Victory, Mata announced the end of his playing career with a poignant video filmed inside a dressing room to the sound of Elvis Presley's 'Now or Never'.

In the clip, Mata symbolically hangs his boots on a hook in the locker room before leaving, with the video captioned: 'Sometimes, to love is to let go.

Sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq

Juan Mata has announced his retirement from football with a poignant video message (Source: Juan Mata)

The former Chelsea and Man United midfielder enjoyed a decorated career on English soil

A popular presence wherever he plied his trade, Mata's comments on social media were soon flooded with well-wishes from former clubs.

'Great player, better person,' Man United shared under his post on X. 'Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan (red heart emoji).'

Chelsea had a similar send-off for him, with the club writing: 'So many special memories. Thank you, Juan (blue heart emoji).'

Former Chelsea executive Marina Granovskaia added her personal thanks with a message too, writing: 'Great video! Great career too! (red heart emoji). Wishing you all the best Juan (blue heart emoji).'

Former team-mates including Ander Herrera, Ashley Young, Santi Cazorla and Mario Suarez were among those to send messages of thanks and congratulations, with Man City star Vivianne Miedema also writing to Mata.

'Congratulations on an amazing career and changing football on and off the pitch (hand clap emoji, green heart emoji),' the Dutch WSL trailblazer wrote.

Despite starting his youth career at Real Madrid, Mata's first senior minutes in the Spanish top flight came with his move in 2007 to Valencia.

Mata notched up 174 appearances for the side and won the Copa del Rey in club colours before his landmark move to Chelsea.

In west London, the midfielder won the FA Cup and Champions League in his first season, and the Europa League in his second.

The video contained a brief farewell message and was widely liked by his former team-mates

After leaving Chelsea, the Spaniard enjoyed a strong stint at Manchester United

At the end of last month, the Euro 2012 winner was treated to a lap of appreciation at his last club Melbourne Victory

But a falling-out with then-coach Jose Mourinho called time on his stint at Stamford Bridge and a move north to join Man United – where he would later reunite with the Portuguese manager during his stint in Manchester between 2016 and 2018.

Mata later enjoyed stints at Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before his move to Melbourne.

In recent years, however, Mata has expanded his career away from the pitch, with the player serving as a pundit at this year's World Cup for ITV, and at the 2024 European Championship for BBC Sport.

As well as appearing in the media, Mata is a keen investor in sporting ventures including Spanish club Real Oviedo, San Diego FC in the MLS and Formula One's Alpine racing team.

Alongside Italy icon Giorgio Chiellini, Mata is an investor in Mercury/13, a women's multi-club ownership group that invests in FC Como Women.

Mata is also a co-owner of Melbourne Victory, with plans to chair a football committee at the club after hanging up his boots.

As well as a shrewd businessman, Mata is also a philanthropist – and was recognised for his donations with an MBE in June 2025.

In 2017, Mata pledged one per cent of his salary to a charitable movement called Common Goal, which supports football charities.

#1475. Kean’s new tibia injury rules former Juventus striker out of Como v Juventus

Moise Kean has broken down again in Como training, three weeks after treatment that was meant to fix his shin. The former Juventus striker is set to miss about two more months, so he will not face his old club on 29 November.

Moise Kean has suffered a new tibia injury in training with Como. The former Juventus striker is now undergoing further medical tests. Sky Sport Italia reported that he will be out for about two more months. That timeline rules him out of Como’s home game against Juventus.

Como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date. The club promised an update once more information was available.

The new problem follows a treatment that was meant to end his shin trouble. On 30 October, Como’s update described his treatment at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona as successful. The club put his recovery at about five weeks. His progress was to be reviewed every day.

That plan has now collapsed. Kean had been out since early October. The original injury came while he was playing for Italy against France on 2 October. That match was the first leg of a Nations League tie.

The setback is a heavy blow for Como. In Serie A, his outings for the club added up to 160 minutes. He has yet to score, including in his single Champions League game. He joined from Fiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent. At Fiorentina he scored 27 league goals in two seasons, 19 of them in 2024/25. Before that, he came through the Juventus academy.

Without him, Como will have to rely on Douvikas up front. The club may also look for a striker in January.

For Juventus, the news removes one threat from a crucial stretch. Como are their next opponents after Venezia. The game is the Sunday evening fixture a week later, in round 13 of Serie A. Kick-off is at 20:45.

Como 1907 is pleased to announce the signing of Italian international forward Moise Kean from @acffiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent.

Luciano Spalletti’s side need results. Juventus sit six points behind fourth place and have averaged just over 1.6 points per game, according to Corriere dello Sport. The paper sees the run of fixtures as decisive for the push for a Champions League place. It warns that dropping points against Venezia would force Juventus to win every remaining game of 2026 to stay in touch with the top four.

The schedule offers little respite after the trip to Como. Juventus host Udinese on 6 December and Monza on 14 December. They then travel to Roma on 19 December.

The series lasted all summer and did not have the epilogue desired by the player, who was very touched or even dejected by the situation. The weeks have passed and Julian Alvarez has digested his immense disappointment at not having joined FC Barcelona during the transfer window. For openly declaring his desire to leave, he was punished by his own supporters, who did not fail to boo him at the start of the season. Until things gradually return to normal.

But inevitably, the reception of the Blaugrana on Sunday evening had symbolic significance for the 26-year-old Argentine striker, established by his coach Diego Simeone. If he was decisive on Giuliano Simeone’s goal, he could blame himself for his two missed opportunities, which could have offered victory to his team, now relegated to 3rd place in Liga.

Obviously, the Spanish press had its eyes on him on Sunday evening, and it is not kind to the Spider. “Julian returns to hell”written as follows Marca. “Julián was completely dejected by this evening, when everything seemed to work in his favor so that he was almost completely forgiven for his summer dream with this same team”note A.S. on his side. His coach defended him after the match.

“He played an important match, he was involved in three other actions in addition to his assist for Giuliano. And the center for Baena was also his. We all wanted this goal, but we will wait because he is a great player and to achieve our goals, we need the best Julián, otherwise we will not succeed.explained Diego Simeone, as confirmation that everything is not yet back to normal for his player, whistled by part of the public after his second miss.

#1472. The Premier League out of contract XI featuring Bruno Fernandes

The January transfer window will soon be upon us, which means a number of clubs will have to decide what to do with their out-of-contract players.

January represents the final chance for clubs to recoup any kind of fee before their players leave on a free in the summer, and there are a number of notable Premier League stars with deals set to expire.

For now, Alisson is leaving in the summer but the goalkeeper has said publicly he wishes to stay.

He has been at Anfield for eight years, solidifying a previous position of weakness for the club, and has a shout for being the best Premier League goalkeeper of all time.

But he is 34 now and does look less mobile than in earlier years.

He’s on £250k a week, the best-paid goalkeeper in the league, and Liverpool may want to get that off their wage bill but Alisson’s case is helped by the lack of an obvious replacement.

Caoimhin Kelleher was sold to Brentford while Giorgi Mamardashvili has not overly impressed in the chances he has been given.

The Bournemouth stalwart is out of contract this summer having joined 13 years ago.

The Cherries did have his replacement last season in Alex Jimenez but had to drop their new signing for off-field issues. He was loaned to Fiorentina while Bournemouth brought in Juanlu Sanchez but he has played just 18 minutes of football so far.

This has led to 35-year-old Smith being first choice in the team.

The club captain signed a one-year extension last summer but there is currently no talk of another new deal.

Depending on who you believe, Van Dijk is either close to signing a new deal or has one foot out the door.

The Liverpool skipper’s contract expires at the end of the season and no one is 100% sure if either club or player are looking to extend the relationship.

Van Dijk is still a commanding presence in Liverpool’s back line but is 35 now and is on £350k a week, the second-highest wage in the Premier League.

Liverpool would likely offer only another 12 months and so maybe Van Dijk will seek a new challenge at a club willing to offer him longer.

There are a whole host of centre-backs out of contract in the summer with Dan Burn, Calvin Bassey, Joe Gomez, Fabian Schar, Ben Davies, Michael Keane and Chris Richards all approaching the end but perhaps the most interesting one to watch is Lisandro Martinez.

Having criticised United’s director of football Jason Wilcox over a lack of recruitment, Martinez may well find himself heading out the door to make room for those improvements.

The club do have the option to extend the deal past the summer but are reportedly in two minds about it considering the outburst. The future of the player will likely depend on Mauricio Pochettino’s view of him.

26% of Palace’s squad is out of contract in the summer, which does not seem the best of planning.

One of the most notable is first-choice left-back Tyrick Mitchell, who is reportedly on the radar of Manchester United and Liverpool.

Palace have the option of extending it a further 12 months but are currently in talks to tie him down to a new deal. Failure to do that and Palace could have another Guehi situation on their hands in the near future.

Ayari is coming towards the end of the four-and-a-half-year deal he signed to first join Brighton back in 2023, although the club do have the option to extend it for a further year.

Contract talks over a new deal are not going well apparently, with Ayari yet to commit to anything as he wishes to keep his options open.

The standout performer of the season so far only returned to Brighton in January and penned an 18-month deal with his former club.

That seemed a wise move for a player who will be 36 come the end of it but his current form makes the option of an extension hard to ignore.

If Brighton, who usually have these things planned out, do offer him a new deal, you suspect it will be for another 12 months rather than committing to a long-term deal for an ageing player.

Europe’s top 10 chance creators in 2026-27: Yamal, Guler, Olise all trail surprise leader

Fernandes has reportedly already rejected two offers from United but the club do have the right to extend it for a further 12 months.

However, extending the deal of a player who has indicated a desire to leave would not sit well with Fernandes, who has a lot of political capital at Old Trafford.

As for the player, he is 32 now and one League Cup, one FA Cup, one Portuguese Cup and two Portuguese League Cups is not the kind of trophy cabinet that reflects his ability.

He may fancy moving to a different club, one where trophies are more assured, but United look determined to ensure that does not happen until 2028 at the earliest.

Murphy has been at Newcastle for almost 10 years having been signed by Rafa Benitez, which seems a remarkable fact.

His contract is due to expire in the summer with Everton and Nottingham Forest rumoured to be interested, but a loss of many senior players has reportedly prompted Matthias Jaissle to ask the club to keep hold of Murphy.

The Mail says talks are “accelerating” on a new deal and Murphy, despite being 31, is even being offered improved terms.

Having looked to legally get his contract ripped up in the summer, Mateta will have a much easier route out of Selhurst Park in 2027.

Mateta has been eager to leave Palace for a while now, making it as far as an AC Milan medical before a knee injury collapsed that move.

He is back in the Palace squad now, playing four games this season, but has yet to score and has picked up a red card.

He’s a decent Premier League striker with double digits of goals in the last three seasons but at 29 years of age, he will probably not be sought after by the very top end of clubs.

Mitoma has been on the sidelines since May with a hamstring injury that required surgery.

Understandably, the Seagulls are being careful with his rehab and so it is only this weekend that he is thought to be in contention for the squad.

Pre-injury, Mitoma was one of Brighton’s best players but it feels like the team has evolved a lot since then and there is always a bit of doubt over how a player returns from such a lengthy absence.

His contract expires in the summer and there have been rumours of a departure for two years now, with the Japanese international reportedly wanting Champions League football.

But with his injury, a Champions League club may not want to take the risk and the Seagulls could be in the competition themselves next season.

If he comes back and performs well, it is likely you would expect him to extend beyond the summer.

#1469. Mauricio Pochettino's Man United rallying cry: New boss promises fans it will be a 'SPECIAL' season - despite club sitting in drop zone - as he gets straight to work after flying from US

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 16:51 EST, 18 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.

The new Red Devils head coach landed in Manchester on Wednesday morning, hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss.

And during a busy first day among his new surroundings, the Argentine sent a direct message to the club's fanbase as he preached for unity.

'Hi Reds, here's it's Mauricio Pochettino,' he said via a video posted on United's X account at 7.15pm on Wednesday evening.

'I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

'I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

A message from Mauricio 💬❤️🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/2lBLkMaGY6

Mauricio Pochettino addressed Manchester United fans directly on Wednesday evening after starting work officially as their new head coach

The new Red Devils head coach has promised a 'special season' in a direct message to fans

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday

'This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players to fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.'

In a second message in his native Spanish, Pochettino expanded further: 'This message is about being united, like the name Manchester United. We all need to work together.

'I hope to bring the happy moments that this club deserves and create the unity that every team needs so that the players can be at their best on the pitch.'

Those messages came less than eight hours after arriving in England. He landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff.

Speaking to the club's media channels earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino said: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.'

The club then officially welcomed the new manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.'

Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening.

He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati.

But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers.

Earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour

The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am

The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino)

'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.'

'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.'

Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge.

Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's new-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford.

'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.

'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something important for the future of soccer in this country.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United

'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made new friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.'

Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change.

An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning.

In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.'

Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to quickly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle.

Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note

The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino said after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'

Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a new contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup.

The quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'

Neil El Aynaoui has recovered from his injury and is ready to return to action for Leipzig.

The Moroccan midfielder, who left the national team’s training camp early due to leg problems, has received the green light from the German club’s medical staff.

According to BILD, the 2001-born player will be available to Martin Demichelis for the away match against Union Berlin, scheduled for Saturday, November 21st.

El Aynaoui had already resumed partial training with his teammates earlier this week, while sporting director Sebastian Schuppan had ruled out any serious issues in recent days: “It’s not a serious injury. According to BILD, if he continues at this level, a buyout at the end of the season could become a possibility. Leipzig paid Roma €4 million for the loan of El Aynaoui, with a buyout option set at €25 million.

#1466. How Claudio Ranieri’s Roma nearly scuppered Inter’s legendary treble

“He’s right with what he said I am very demanding of myself and I have to win to be sure of things. This is why I have won so many trophies in my career,” was Jose Mourinho’s humble retort to Claudio Ranieri in the early months of his tenure at Inter.

“Ranieri on the other hand has the mentality of someone who doesn’t need to win.

“He is almost 70 years old. He has won a Super Cup and another small trophy, and he is too old to change his mentality. He’s old and he hasn’t won anything.”

Ranieri was in fact only 56 at the time – something that Mourinho almost certainly knew. Now – 16 years later – he is actually 73 if Mourinho feels like a more accurate rehash.

“I studied Italian five hours a day for many months to ensure I could communicate with the players, media and fans,” Mourinho added. “Ranieri had been in England for five years and still struggled to say ‘good morning’ and ‘good afternoon.'”

While Mourinho was cementing his status as A Special One at Chelsea – doing what his predecessor couldn’t quite manage – by converting Roman Abramovich’s millions into major honours, Ranieri saw his reputation flounder with short and unsuccessful stints in charge of Valencia and Parma.

Still, the Italian was entrusted to take the reigns at newly-promoted Juventus in 2007 following Didier Deschamps’ falling out with the board. He inherited a squad boasting Gianluigi Buffon, Giorgio Chiellini, Pavel Nedved, David Trezeguet and Alessandro Del Piero as the Old Lady looked to quickly heal the scars of Calciopoli.

Ranieri led Juventus to a respectable third-place finish in their first season back, with a remit to go those couple of steps further as Mourinho – back then the sexiest name in football management – arrived to take the helm at champions Inter in 2008.

Juve did make a step forward – second, not third – but the goals had dried up as Trezeguet spent most of the campaign sidelined with a groin injury. Inter had enough about them – with a prime Zlatan Ibrahimovic banging in the goals – to continue their domestic dominance with Mourinho in charge, cruising to a fourth successive Scudetto with a 10-point lead.

Inter’s Portuguese coach was at his spikiest and most self-assured, refusing to shirk away from any verbal battles if he felt slighted by journalists or rival coaches.

Not for the first time, Ranieri found himself in Mourinho’s crosshairs during a wide-ranging rant at the media, Roma, Milan and Juve after a controversial decision to award Mario Balotelli a penalty in a 3-3 draw with Roma.

“There has been the greatest amount of intellectual manipulation. There was a concerted, organised effort to manipulate public opinion. It was fantastic work but it is unrelated to my world – I work in football,” Mourinho claimed as Inter approached the finishing line in 2009.

“I don’t like intellectual prostitution, I like honesty. Over the last few days nobody has mentioned that Roma have great players but will end the season without a title. Nobody has mentioned that Milan have 11 fewer points than us and will end the season without a title.

“Nobody has spoken about Juventus, who have won so many points thanks to refereeing mistakes. We have only won one game thanks to a mistake and that was the Siena match.

“Ranieri said he is shoulder to shoulder with Luciano Spalletti? Well, I will side with all the coaches who have fallen foul against Juventus – Cesare Prandelli, Pasquale Marino, Gigi Del Neri.”

Mourinho responded to the media, Spalleti and Ranieri who accused Mario Balotelli of being a diver, when Inter drew 3-3 with the Spalleti’s Roma. 🤯 pic.twitter.com/u3AeMPpVOs

— Sir José #Giallorossi (@MourinhoTheGOAT) May 24, 2020

Ranieri was sacked shortly before the end of the 2008-09 campaign after Juventus went tumbling out of the title race in a run of seven winless matches, while Mourinho signed a contract extension to commit his future at the San Siro.

As Mourinho was gearing up for a second season in charge, a rising Juventus, with Fabio Cannavaro making an ill-fated return following three years at the Bernabeu, were still being talked up as Inter’s likeliest challengers. Carlo Ancelotti and Kaka had left Milan, while Roma finished a distant sixth.

Luciano Spaletti had led Roma to the Supercoppa and Coppa Italia, as well a runner-up finish in Serie A, during the 2007-08 season, but they struggled to maintain the same standards the following year. After Roma started the 2009-10 season with back-to-back defeats to Genoa and Juve, Spaletti resigned.

After a summer off, Ranieri promptly found himself back in a job – at his hometown club, who he’d grown up supporting. But few if any pundits expected Roma to seriously compete with the journeyman coach at the helm – not least Mourinho, who evidently didn’t consider Ranieri a rival, every passing mention dripping with patronising contempt.

“Everyone knows that Ranieri is not a top-class coach, but he will not be expected to win the Scudetto. The target at the moment is middle-tier, so Roma have gone for a middle-tier coach,” wrote GOAL Italia’s editor Sergio Stanco in an op-ed reacting to the appointment.

And when the Giallorossi lost three Serie A matches in a row in late October in a series of fraught battles full of bookings and red cards, Roma found themselves down in 14th, two points clear of the relegation zone.

The only question was whether they could salvage a Europa League place, let alone mount a title push – Inter had started the season like a train and were 14 points clear after 10 matches.

What happened next, against all the odds, was one of the most thrilling and hard-fought title races that European football has ever seen.

READ: Comparing Claudio Ranieri’s eight best teams: Fiorentina, Chelsea, Leicester…

Slowly but surely, Ranieri’s Roma began to find form, holding table-topping Inter to a 1-1 draw at the San Siro as they kicked off a 24-match unbeaten run. Come to the winter break, they were up to fourth – but 11 points behind Mourinho’s league leaders.

In the new year, Roma began to mix dazzling performances with gritty 1-0 wins. They looked like a title-winning side. Mirko Vucinic and Francesco Totti were routinely producing match-winning displays, while Daniele De Rossi was at the peak of his powers, looking every bit a world-class midfielder.

Ranieri’s men took 40 of the first 48 points available, winning 12 and drawing four, following the winter break. All the while Juventus were plummeting down to midtable obscurity since their decision to dismiss him.

Meanwhile, Inter were faltering. Their comfortable lead was getting whittled away. They failed to win back-to-back matches between January and April and were constantly dropping points on their travels, failing to win at Bari, Parma, Napoli, Catania, Palermo and Fiorentina.

Come late March, and their visit to the Stadio Olimpico, Inter’s season looked on the verge of complete collapse. Mourinho’s man for the moment Diego Milito cancelled out De Rossi’s early opener, but Luca Toni – during a memorable half-season loan from Bayern Munich – came up with an iconic match-winner that resulted in one of the loudest roars in the history of the Eternal City. No Gladiator could muster a moment like this.

FLASHBACK | 💥 | On this day in 2010… a classic finish from Luca Toni secured victory against Inter Milan! 👋#ASRoma pic.twitter.com/NjMdSyLaQs

— AS Roma English (@ASRomaEN) March 27, 2018

All season, Ranieri had played down his side’s chances of doing the impossible, just as he’d done at Juventus and just as he’d do at Leicester. But once Roma moved within a point of the top spot with seven games to go, the tinkerman allowed himself to dream.

“We’re out of the last bend and now we are on the final straight, one metre behind Inter,” said Ranieri after their 2-1 victory over Inter.

“We have reopened the title race, now it will be a test of nerves. For five months we have chased and sacrificed ourselves to the cause; now we have beaten a stratospheric team who deserve our compliments.”

An early Europa League exit to Panathinaikos at the first knockout hurdle allowed Roma to focus on domestic matters, while Inter were going deep into the Champions League.

Not only did the Giallorossi stand in Inter’s way in Serie A – even briefly usurping them to the top spot in April, with five games to go – but they were also their opponents in the Coppa Italia final.

But it was at this point, with their backs to the wall and in stark danger of crashing and burning, that Mourinho’s Inter did what the truly great sides do and stood up to produce some of their greatest performances when they needed to.

The counter-attacking masterclasses served to Barcelona and Bayern Munich in the semis and final of the Champions League were their most famous victories, but they were pushed to be every bit as good back home as the league and cup went down to the wire.

Milito, as he so often did in the defining games at the business end of Inter’s historic treble, came up with the decisive intervention and notched the only goal of the game in the Coppa final at the Olimpico, while a frustrated Totti was shown red in the dying moments.

After going top with three points against Atalanta, Ranieri’s Roma held onto their place at the summit the following week in a full-blooded derby against Lazio, peppered by 12 yellow cards and one red but most importantly a 2-1 win.

But a week later they succumbed to a 2-1 defeat at home to Sampdoria. Totti had given Roma an early lead, but a second-half brace from Giampaolo Pazzini was enough to blow their title hopes. Just as you’d be brave to mention Steven Gerrard’s slip in the red half of Merseyside, Pazzini is a name best avoided in Rome.

Iconic image of Mexes crying on the Roma bench was 10 years ago today. The infamous Roma-Samp pazzini game. The game that cost Roma the scudetto #ASRoma pic.twitter.com/R6yfaxo4eW

— Scot Munroe (@scot_munroe) April 25, 2020

It was Roma’s only defeat of their last 28 in Serie A, while they won eight of the last nine, but it was enough to cost them. Inter took advantage by winning their last five in a row, taking 19 of 21 points on offer after their defeat in the capital.

History is written by the victors, after all, leaving Roma to be remembered as one of the great nearly sides and Ranieri destined to be a nearly man – until Leicester, of course.

It was Ranieri’s miracle Foxes, after all, that inflicted a 2-1 victory on Mourinho’s Chelsea in December 2015, keeping them at the top of the table and their opponents just a point above the relegation zone.

Mourinho was then sacked, but – water under the bridge, apparently – he showed support to Ranieri following his dismissal at the King Power the following year, wearing CR on his training top in his press conference.

Ranieri returned to Roma for an emergency two-month spell at the end of the 2018-19 season. “Mr. Ranieri, in our moment of dire need, you have answered. Now, you receive the homage of your people,” read one banner and the veteran coach struggled to hold back the tears on the touchline in his first game back in charge at the Olimpico.

He later returned for a third stint, once again in their hour of need during the 2024-25 campaign.

Mourinho has since done something Ranieri never quite could and delivered silverware for the Giallorossi. But he never quite surpassed the love the Eternal City has for one of its favourite sons.

Federico Chiesa could leave Liverpool as early as January, with Roma remaining among the clubs interested in bringing him back to Italy.

According to Calciomercato.com, the striker is considering a change of team to regain consistency, after another first half of the season spent almost entirely on the sidelines for the English club.

The 1997-born striker played just two minutes in the Premier League, coming on as a late substitute against Manchester City on October 11th.

Having arrived from Juventus in the summer of 2024, Chiesa has made 51 appearances and scored five goals for Liverpool, failing to secure a regular starting spot even after Andoni Iraola took over as manager.

#1461. Man Utd predicted XI vs. Liverpool for Pochettino’s first game in charge

We’re finally ready to get our first glimpse of a Mauricio Pochettino Manchester United team as the new head coach prepares for his debut in the dugout against Liverpool on Sunday.

It’s a big one to kick off the Pochettino era, with United travelling to Anfield to face their long-time rivals Liverpool. The prospect of a Pochettino-led Man Utd side has been a hypothetical for years and now it’s finally going to become a reality. But what will its first version look like?

There’s only so much you can guess from drones being flown over training. Pochettino was seen speaking closely with a group including Harry Amass and Joshua Zirkzee in the leaked footage and we’d be stunned if either got their first start of the season in the league in such a big game.

It’s more likely that Pochettino will be sticking with the tried and trusted for now. Well, maybe not so trusted anymore given United’s recent form under Michael Carrick, but it’s Pochettino’s job to change that outlook.

Like his predecessor, Pochettino usually favours a 4-2-3-1 formation. It’ll probably be the starting point for his first United lineup, although who fits into it remains to be seen.

There are some safer bets. Senne Lammens in goal, Bruno Fernandes in attacking midfield, Bryan Mbeumo – who’ll be making his 50th appearance for the club – somewhere in attack. These things rarely change, regardless of who’s in charge.

What Pochettino will have to weigh up more carefully is whether to throw his compatriot Lisandro Martinez back into defence as he returns from suspension. The suspicion is that he will.

Moreover, he might have Luke Shaw – his former Southampton prodigy – back from injury to select at left-back. If not, Patrick Dorgu took part in Pochettino’s first training session, which is promising.

The new boss will also hope to be able to call on Harry Maguire, who’s been back in training after a back issue.

Midfielder Carlos Baleba and striker Benjamin Sesko remain out for the foreseeable future with their injuries. Marcus Rashford is still a doubt as well, but isn’t too far off a comeback.

Here’s how we reckon Pochettino will set his side up for his first game in charge.

#1459. Gasperini previews Parma-Roma: “Dybala and Svilar are back.”

Roma is ready to return to action after the international break.

The Giallorossi will fly to the Tardini to face Alberto Gilardino’s Parma, who spoke on the eve of the match about his relationship with the Grugliasco-born coach. The Giallorossi coach spoke at a press conference one day before the match against Parma.

“Dybala and Svilar trained well. They have fully recovered. Pellegrini, who will have a longer return, and Rensch, who has started training with good intensity, are left out.”

“Last year’s comeback against Parma was crucial; it opened the doors to the Champions League for us. It was a fundamental step. This new season is different; the objectives are emerging along the way.”

“As for the transfer market, it’s appropriate for the CEO to speak about it. If necessary, he’ll be the one to say what Roma can do on the market, which is always a complicated and difficult one.”

“Soule? Clearly, travel and time zones have an impact. We’ll try to figure it out this afternoon during the final training session, including for Balerdi and Castro. We left Soulé in extraordinary condition, but we have three important matches. Soulé isn’t a problem; the important thing is that he’s injury-free.”

“Dybala? I don’t know his condition. We’ll see what happens as we play. It’s true he hasn’t played for a month, but sooner or later he’ll have to play, and we’ll evaluate him during the match. He’s recovered physically, so we’ll see how he’s doing from time to time.”

“Having Soulé and Dybala at our disposal is a strength. Soulé has reached a high level of quality, he’s been called up to the Argentina squad. He’s evolving, like Mora. They’re players who are growing, the important thing is to have them. Dybala and Soulé are a great fit; coexistence is a false problem.”

On the strength of the squad, despite the many absences. “We’ve had strong performances from other players, which have helped us avoid feeling the impact of the absences. We have to look ahead; the break always leaves you with some doubts. You think you can restart with the certainties of Sassuolo, but that’s not the case. There have been constant breaks lately, and some players have played less. So it’s also an individual assessment, especially regarding the first matchday. We need to get back on track immediately. Tomorrow is a tough match; the standings are starting to become more clear, and points are starting to count for more.”

“I don’t think there are any definitive transfer market situations today. There are still a lot of games to go, and players who aren’t playing can play more, or vice versa. We’re in constant conversation with D’Amico, but there’s been no transfer planning other than between the two of us.”
